title: Observability and Operational Governance
readerIntent: Understand how Nodics exposes health, evidence, governed changes, and recovery across modules.
owner: Runtime lifecycle, diagnostics, audit, health, and nDynamo governance capabilities
summary: Logs, metrics, traces, health, readiness, audit, and governed runtime changes let operators understand and control independently deployed modules without creating new authorities.

sections.heading: What is Observability and Operational Governance?
paragraphs: Observability is the ability to understand a running system through logs, metrics, traces, health signals, and audit evidence. Operational governance defines who may change runtime behavior, how that change is approved, and how operators recover when a change or dependency fails.

It is the combination of an aircraft instrument panel and its operating procedures: signals reveal current conditions, while governed controls prevent an operator from making an untracked or unsafe adjustment.

sections.heading: Operational outcomes
items: Know whether a process is live, ready, degraded, draining, stopped, or failed.
Trace a request, job, event, workflow, publication, import, provider call, and runtime change across module boundaries.
Preview, approve, activate, audit, clean up, and roll back eligible runtime contracts.
Diagnose failures without exposing secrets or sensitive payloads.

sections.heading: Authority
items: nConfig owns the single process lifecycle and signal handling.
Each module/provider contributes bounded readiness, drain, and shutdown hooks.
nDynamo governs only supported runtime-mutable contracts; static layered configuration remains authoritative.
BackOffice, MCP, CLI, and AI tools call these contracts and never become mutation authorities.

sections.heading: Why this matters to a business
items: A modular platform is useful only when operators can distinguish a healthy process from one that merely accepts a TCP connection. Readiness protects customers from partially initialized modules and unavailable required dependencies.

Graceful drain reduces interrupted requests and duplicated scheduled work during deployment. Durable ownership, idempotency, and reconciliation protect work that cannot be completed inside a process shutdown hook.

Governed runtime changes let authorized teams adjust supported behavior without rebuilding while retaining preview, approval, provenance, audit, rollback, and protection of static or secret configuration.
Consistent correlation across APIs, jobs, events, workflows, imports, publications, caches, search, and providers shortens incident diagnosis without creating a second observability authority.

sections.heading: Example and readiness evidence
items: When a CMS node restarts during a campaign, the load balancer stops sending new traffic after readiness becomes false, in-flight work drains within policy, and other replicas continue serving.

BackOffice registration is optional control-plane work and retries asynchronously after startup. Its outage does not block customer traffic, while a missing required database dependency prevents readiness.

Evidence includes lifecycle state transitions, hook duration, rejected work during drain, durable work recovery, registration retry, correlated safe telemetry, configuration activation audit, and rollback outcome.

Acceptance covers normal startup, partial dependencies, signal handling, timeout, crash, OOM assumptions, duplicate ownership, multi-node coordination, provider outage, incident recovery, and regression.
